::: {.callout-note}
## Learning objectives

- Name three things a bash driver script cannot tell you after a change.
- Describe a workflow as a graph of files and the steps that make them.
- Explain what "working backward from the targets" means.
- Know what you will build in this course and where the lab's pipelines fit.

Time: 20 min
:::

## The script you already have

Most analyses in the lab start like this. The course ships one in
`snakemakeify/`: nine scripts and a driver that runs them in order.

```{.bash filename="snakemakeify/run_all.sh"}
#!/bin/bash
# Whole HCT116 analysis, start to finish. Run from an empty folder:
#   mkdir -p ~/snakemakeify/legacy && cd ~/snakemakeify/legacy
#   bash ~/snakemake-course/snakemakeify/run_all.sh 2>&1 | tee run_all.log
# Each step skips samples it has already done, so it is safe to re-run.

SCRIPTS=$(dirname $0)

echo "== 01 fastqc";   bash $SCRIPTS/01_fastqc.sh
echo "== 02 align";    bash $SCRIPTS/02_align.sh
echo "== 03 filter";   bash $SCRIPTS/03_filter.sh
echo "== 04 peaks";    bash $SCRIPTS/04_call_peaks.sh
...
```

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}
It works. It runs on the real course data and produces peaks, tracks and a
figure. The trouble starts the second time you run it, after you change
something.
:::

## "Safe to re-run"

Each step decides for itself whether to do any work. This is the loop in
`03_filter.sh`:

```{.bash filename="snakemakeify/03_filter.sh"}
for s in $SAMPLES; do
    if [ -f $s.filt.bam ]; then
        echo "$s already filtered, skipping"
        continue
    fi
    ...
    samtools view -b -q $MAPQ $s.bam > $s.q$MAPQ.bam
```

The check asks one question: does the output exist? It never asks whether the
output is still correct.

::: {.notes}
Ask the room before showing the next slide: "I change MAPQ from 30 to 20 and
run run_all.sh again. What happens?" Most people say "it refilters". It does
not.
:::

## What the driver cannot tell you

Suppose you lower `MAPQ` from 30 to 20 in `03_filter.sh` and run the driver
again.

- Every sample already has a `.filt.bam`, so step 03 skips all ten.
- Step 04 finds the old peak files and skips too.
- `06_qc_summary.py` has no skip check, so it writes a fresh table today, from
  the old MAPQ 30 files.

You now have a QC table with a new date and old numbers. To get it right you
have to know which files depend on the filtered BAMs, delete them by hand, and
rerun. The dependency chain lives in your head, not in the code.

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}
There are quieter problems too. `02_align.sh` pipes `bowtie2` into
`samtools sort` without `set -o pipefail`, so if bowtie2 dies halfway, the
pipe still exits 0 and leaves a short BAM behind. The next run sees the BAM,
skips the sample, and the truncated file flows into everything downstream.
Nothing records which version of the script or which settings made a file.
And moving the driver to the cluster means rewriting it as a set of `sbatch`
jobs that wait for each other.
:::

## Turn it around: start from the files

A workflow manager asks a different question. Instead of "run these steps in
this order", you say "I want these files", and give it rules for how each kind
of file is made.

```text
I want output/consensus/CTCF_consensus.bed
  -> made from the CTCF peak files of both replicates
     -> each made from a filtered BAM and its control's filtered BAM
        -> each made from an aligned BAM
           -> made from a FASTQ and the bowtie2 index
```

Snakemake builds that chain for every file you ask for, then runs only the
steps whose outputs are missing or out of date. This is what
"working backward from the targets" means.

## The graph

Every chain together forms a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of jobs. This is the
rule graph of the finished course pipeline, one box per rule:

{{< generated name="regpipe-rulegraph" alt="Rule graph of RegPipe: fastqc, bowtie2_index, align, filter, call_peaks, consensus_peaks, bigwig, frip, qc_table, ctcf_rad21_overlap, locus_plot and enhancer_activity feeding rule all" width="90%" >}}

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}
You never write the graph. Snakemake works it out by matching the input files
of one rule to the output files of another. The same pipeline on ten samples
is 61 jobs; you will see those counts in the dry runs from module 1 on.
:::

## What the lab gets from it

Reruns
: Change a setting and Snakemake reruns the jobs that used it, and every job
  downstream of them. Nothing else. In module 4 you change the MAPQ cutoff
  and watch the dry run list the filter jobs and the peak calls after them.

Provenance
: Snakemake records which rule, command, parameters and software environment
  made each file. `snakemake --summary` prints it per file. A failed job's
  half-written outputs are deleted, so a truncated BAM does not survive.

Cluster
: The same Snakefile runs on your laptop and on SLURM. What changes is a
  profile (module 5), not the rules.

::: {.notes}
The provenance point is the one people care about later. When a reviewer asks
"which MAPQ cutoff did you use for figure 3", the answer is in the config file
that made it, not in someone's memory.
:::

## Where the course goes

You build **RegPipe** on public HCT116 data from ENCODE: CTCF and H3K27ac
ChIP-seq with their inputs, and DNase-seq, all trimmed to a 5 Mb window of
chr8 around *MYC* (chr8:125,000,000-130,000,000). The window is small enough
that the whole pipeline runs on a laptop in a couple of minutes.

| Day | Modules | You end with |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0-4 | aligned and filtered BAMs, peaks, consensus peaks, bigWigs (stopping point B) |
| 2 | 5-8 | profiles for the cluster, a split-up pipeline, R and Python steps, tests (stopping point D) |

The finished RegPipe has the same layout as the lab's MicroCPipe, TTpipe and
ChromSimPipe, so the [field guide](../field-guide/index.qmd) reads those
pipelines with the ideas you just learned.

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}
If you fall behind at any point, copy the folder of the last stopping point
(`stopping-points/stopA/` to `stopD/`) and keep going. The
[schedule](../schedule.qmd) shows where each one falls.
:::

## Exercise

::: {.callout-tip .exercise}
## Exercise 0.1: Draw the chain for one file

Open `snakemakeify/04_call_peaks.sh`. On paper, draw the files that have to
exist before `peaks/HCT116_CTCF_1_peaks.narrowPeak` can be made, back to the
raw FASTQs. Mark which script makes each file.

Then suppose you delete `HCT116_input-CTCF_1.bam` and run `run_all.sh` again,
so that one BAM is made fresh. Which files in your drawing are now out of
date? Which of them does `run_all.sh` actually remake?

[Answer](../answers/00-why-answers.qmd#ex-0.1)
:::

## Key points

- A driver script runs steps in order. It does not know which files depend on
  which, so after a change you have to work that out yourself.
- "The output exists" is not the same as "the output is up to date".
- Snakemake works backward from the files you ask for, through rules that say
  how each kind of file is made, and runs only what is missing or stale.
- The graph of those dependencies is the DAG. You describe the rules;
  Snakemake builds the graph.
